body:
## Problem

Sepo records repository visibility at canonical deploy time in both the preview registry (`isPrivate`) and the deployed R2 `META` (`visibility`). Changing a GitHub repository from private to public, or public to private, does not update either snapshot until another canonical deployment happens.

This can leave a newly public site behind the private-site gate. More importantly, a newly private repository's previously public deployment can remain publicly served until a later deployment.

GitHub exposes repository visibility transitions through the `repository` event actions `publicized` and `privatized`.

## Proposed change

Update `.github/workflows/agent-deploy-site-main.yml` to trigger on visibility changes in addition to its existing triggers:

```yaml
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
  repository:
    types: [publicized, privatized]
```

Ensure the deploy job's guard accepts `repository` events while continuing to deploy only the default branch. The canonical deployment should refresh both the Redis registry record and R2 metadata from GitHub's current repository visibility.

## Acceptance criteria

- A `publicized` event automatically runs the canonical deployment and makes the refreshed site public without a manual dispatch.
- A `privatized` event automatically runs the canonical deployment and gates the refreshed site.
- Existing default-branch push and manual-dispatch behavior remains intact.
- The workflow runs from the repository's default branch and preserves existing concurrency behavior.
- Tests or documentation cover the visibility-event trigger and the expected snapshot-refresh behavior.
- The implementation considers and documents the exposure window while a `privatized` redeployment is running; if a full rebuild is not sufficiently fail-closed, capture a follow-up for a lightweight visibility-refresh path.

comments.body:
I can scope this, but there is one important caveat: GitHub Actions’ documented workflow trigger for private-to-public is `public`, not `repository: types: [publicized]`; I do not see `repository` listed as an Actions workflow event. GitHub’s Actions docs say `public` runs when the repo changes from private to public and runs on the default branch: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows#public

For public-to-private, a repo-local workflow alone may not satisfy the acceptance criteria. GitHub webhook/audit ecosystems may expose repository visibility transitions, but Actions docs do not document a native `privatized` workflow trigger. So the reliable design is:

1. Update [`.github/workflows/agent-deploy-site-main.yml`](.github/workflows/agent-deploy-site-main.yml) to add `public` for private-to-public refreshes.
2. Replace the hardcoded `github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'` guard with a default-branch-aware guard, e.g. compare against `github.event.repository.default_branch`, while preserving `AGENT_ENABLED`.
3. For private-to-public, let the existing full canonical deploy path refresh the Sepo registry `isPrivate` and R2 `META.visibility`, since [`.github/actions/deploy-sepo-site/action.yml`](.github/actions/deploy-sepo-site/action.yml) already sends `canonical: true`.
4. For public-to-private, add or use a service-side GitHub App webhook path that receives the repository visibility event and either dispatches a default-branch canonical deploy or, preferably, calls a lightweight visibility-refresh endpoint before any rebuild.
5. Document the exposure window in [README.md](README.md): a full rebuild is not fail-closed for `privatized` because the previously public deployment can remain public until deploy completes successfully.
6. Add tests in [`.agent/src/__tests__/envelope.test.ts`](.agent/src/__tests__/envelope.test.ts) or workflow validation coverage to assert the `public` trigger, default-branch guard behavior, and docs mention the visibility snapshot refresh.

My recommendation: implement `public` immediately for the publicized case, but treat the privatized case as requiring a backend/lightweight refresh path. A full rebuild-only solution is useful but not strong enough for the security side of the issue because failed or slow builds leave the old public snapshot live.
